inspiration: Table art as one raster per theme, with the felt rectangle centred by a crop plus a centre-mode rule. The theme XML states the felt edges in pixel coordinates and says only the crop shifts the table against the card row. Transfer as a layout rule: the arena backdrop is cropped so its centre matches the action focal point (data/gfx/qml/table/disco/discotablestyle.xml, header comment lines 1-30).

Action buttons keep the same shape for each action but change the material. The pirates theme turns the four action colours into four wood tones with knots, rivets and edge light (data/gfx/qml/table/pirates/piratestablestyle.xml line 16 onward; disco equivalent at line 22). Recreate: one button shape, four material tones matched to role.

Small-size card readability rule: below 75 px the card switches to one large rank glyph and one suit symbol, dropping the detail (data-copyright.txt lines 69-71; src/gui/qt6-qml/resources/cards-simple/). Maps directly onto the 375 wide readability problem for small HUD icons.

Blind and dealer tokens encode state by material and size. The small blind is pale and worn, the big blind rich gold; the dealer is a cast-iron ball with a fuse placed in the free corner so it stays nearly as large as the coins (piratestablestyle.xml line 22 and following). Recreate as target-marking tokens with clearly different materials.

Faceted sphere backdrop built from projected grid facets and gradient glow, not filters, because the renderer cannot do filters (data/gfx/qml/backside/disco/backside.svg header lines 2-4; generator generate_disco_backside.py in repo root, not read). Technique transferable to a glow effect built from gradients only.

Sound design per game event: separate short cues for each action (fold, check, call, raise, bet, all-in, deal), a your-turn beep, and an escalating blind-level stinger with three levels (data/sounds/default/ file names only; audio not opened). Idea: escalating stingers per tier (wave, threat level), recreated from scratch.

Skin packs as data: each table or card-back theme is a folder of art plus one XML style file with a preview image, so themes are added without code changes (data/gfx/qml/table/*/ 20 folders, data/gfx/qml/cards/ 11 folders). Pattern for loot-set or zone skins as data.

briefs.label: Plank-tone action bar
briefs.why: Four action buttons read as physical objects with one shape and four material tones, so the choice is clear even at small size.
briefs.keep: one shared button shape; four tones from one material family; rivet and edge-light details; the role-to-tone map
briefs.change: use stone, iron and bone tones, not timber; change the bevel and corner radius; add a role icon instead of relying on colour alone
briefs.ref: data/gfx/qml/table/pirates/piratestablestyle.xml (line 16 onward, action buttons); disco equivalent data/gfx/qml/table/disco/discotablestyle.xml line 22

briefs.label: Faceted glow ball (gradient-only)
briefs.why: A single faceted sphere with a gradient glow reads at a glance and needs no filters, which suits a fast browser canvas.
briefs.keep: faceted surface from projected grid cells; gradient glow instead of a filter; dark-room lighting
briefs.change: use a shard or crystal form instead of a sphere; a different glow colour and ornament; a moving light pattern instead of a fixed one

briefs.label: Mini-glyph at small size
briefs.why: Below a size threshold the card drops its detail and keeps one large glyph and one symbol, so it stays legible.
briefs.keep: a size threshold that switches to a simplified glyph set; one large mark plus one symbol
briefs.change: use our own threat or target icons, not card ranks; different threshold in pixels for a 375 wide layout

briefs.label: Fuse-token marker
briefs.why: A round marker with an accent placed in the free corner keeps its size when it carries extra detail.
briefs.keep: object placed off-centre so the extra element does not shrink the main body; heavy material read
briefs.change: use a rune-stone or ember marker; a different shape; no fuse
briefs.ref: data/gfx/qml/table/pirates/piratestablestyle.xml (line 22 and the dealer note that follows it)

briefs.label: Escalating level stinger
briefs.why: Three levels of one stinger tell the player the stakes went up without a new tune each time.
briefs.keep: one motif, three steps; the step is tied to a game clock that moves up
briefs.change: our own motif and instrument; tie to wave or threat tier; never reuse the donor's sound file
